method: Primary pages opened and read with the web tool

checks.title: Software intended for a medical purpose
checks.finding: TGA guidance explains that intended purpose determines whether software is a medical device. Regulated software generally needs ARTG inclusion before supply unless excluded or exempt. This does not classify or approve Aura.

checks.title: NDIS age and transition rules
checks.finding: The NDIS page states that applicants must be younger than 65 when applying. Existing participants can choose to continue after 65, with a separate requirement to leave when moving into residential aged care after 65. Other eligibility and item-funding rules also apply.

checks.title: Assessed support at home
checks.finding: My Aged Care confirms Support at Home began in November 2025. Services and funding follow assessment and approval. Its AT-HM scheme separately funds approved assistive technology and home modifications for assessed needs; this is not approval of an Aura product.

checks.title: Assistive technology and home modifications
checks.finding: The AT-HM scheme page describes an aged care assessment, an approval recorded in the person’s decision letter and support plan, and provider involvement for relevant equipment or modifications.

checks.title: Specialist hyperbaric delivery
checks.finding: RBWH describes specialist fitness assessment, qualified medical, nursing and technical delivery, permitted-item restrictions and clinical referral. Its service information does not establish a benefit for the proposed combined Aura programme.

scope: Specific checks only. Not a full independent fact-check of the source introduction.
